description.plain:
Stefani Joanne Angelina Germanotta, better known by her stage name Lady Gaga, is an American singer, songwriter and actress. She is known for her flamboyant fashion statements and live performances. Although her music is easily mistaken as vapid, it often has a self-empowering message.

She started working for Interscope Records when she was 20 years old, writing songs for The Pussycat Dolls, among others. From there, she became one of the biggest pop stars in the world, ranking in numerous #1 albums and singles along with a variety of awards.

She has acted in several movies and TV shows. In 2016, she won a Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Miniseries or Television Film for her portrayal of Elizabeth, a lead character in the fifth season of American Horror Story.

Fun Fact: The “Lady Gaga” moniker was created by her former boyfriend and producer Rob Fusari—he sent a text message with an autocorrected version of Queen’s song “Radio Ga Ga” (a song he sang every time she entered the studio).

description.plain:
In this R&B-esque dance cut, Lady Gaga compares letting the media talk about her any way they want to giving explicit romantic consent. R. Kelly joins in to be the actual lover who she goes to.

Considering the song’s subject matter, the cover art fits, as opposed to being sexual for the sake of marketing.

Due to hitting #1 on iTunes charts all over the world, it was promoted from ARTPOP’s 1st promotional single to the 2nd official single.

Since the song’s release in 2013, R. Kelly’s allegations of sexual abuse and misconduct grew to monumental levels. As a proponent of Gaga proceeded to face criticism as she continued to keep silent on the matter. However, she finally took to Twitter on January 9, 2019, to share a note regarding the situation. She stated her belief in the accusers and support of all victims of sexual assault, denounced R. Kelly and his allegations, and explained how her past experiences and mental capacity at the time led to the song being pushed forward:

The song is called ‘Do What U Want (With My Body)’, I think it’s clear how explicitly twisted my thinking was at the time. If I could go back and have a talk with my younger self I’d tell her to go through the therapy I have since then, so that I could understand the confused post-traumatic state I was in. […] I’m sorry, both for my poor judgment when I was young, and not for speaking out sooner.

She also announced the removal of the song from digital marketplaces and streaming platforms. Two days later on January 11th, the song and remix EP were removed, though the re-release with fellow pop artist Christina Aguilera remains available.

The same day, Christina expressed her support on Twitter:

Being a survivor of past predators myself, these lines spoke to me, which is why I did the song. I embrace all survivors of sexual and domestic violence and abuse holding a special place in my heart, and you @ladygaga, for doing the right thing!

description.plain:
“Bad Romance” represents the Fear of Love Monster from the eight new songs in Lady Gaga’s re-release of The Fame.

Gaga talked to Grazia about writing this record saying:

I was in Russia, then Germany, and spent a lot of time in Eastern Europe. There is this amazing German house-techno music, so I wanted to make a pop experimental record. I kind of wanted to leave the ‘80s a little bit, so the chorus is a '90s melody, which is what the inspiration was. There was certainly some whisky involved in the writing of the record. It’s about being in love with your best friend.

description.plain:
“Sexxx Dreams” was first debuted at Lady Gaga’s iTunes Festival set in September 2013.

The raunchy track sees Gaga initiating an affair with a man’s girlfriend, mixing the lust that haunts Gaga’s dreams with the temptation that the other woman feels.

The track was originally meant to serve as the lead single from ARTPOP, but was replaced with “Applause.” Gaga expanded on the decision during the final episode of her August 2020 podcast Gaga Radio, adding:

The first single from ARTPOP was supposed to be “Sexxx Dreams,” but then I wrote “Applause” and I was like, “No, this one has to be the single!”

The track was originally meant to serve as the lead single from ARTPOP, but was replaced with “Applause.” Gaga expanded on the decision during the final episode of her August 2020 podcast Gaga Radio, adding:

The first single from ARTPOP was supposed to be “Sexxx Dreams,” but then I wrote “Applause” and I was like, “No, this one has to be the single!”

https://twitter.com/ladygaga/status/783715081112719360?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw

description.plain:
Are the rules of sexual attraction akin to the rules of poker? Lady Gaga asserts “Poker Face” is about bisexuality. She described poker face as the expression she pulls when she’s having sex with a man, but wishes she was having sex with a woman.

It was the second single from her debut studio album, The Fame, taking the crown for her most successful single alongside “Just Dance.” The official music video was released on October 22nd, 2008.

“Poker Face” reigns as one of the best-selling singles of all time, with over 14 million copies sold. When it comes to sales in the United States, according to Billboard, as of February 10th, 2019, the song has sold a total of 7.5 million copies. The song climbed to #1 in 20 countries, racking up over 7 million downloads to make it Gaga’s best selling digital single. The track won Gaga her first Grammy for Best Dance Recording at the 52nd Grammy Awards, while it was also nominated for Song of the Year and Record of the Year.

“G.U.Y. (Girl Under You)” is a power-bottom anthem. It was one of the first tracks to be recorded for the album.

Any kind of feminist has valid views for herself about what it means to be a feminist, but, as a new-age feminist, I would say I quite like the transference of strength I feel by submitting to a man – being under him. I actually wrote a song about it on my album, it’s called GUY and it stands for Go Under You. So wearing make-up, smelling delicious and having suckable, kissable, edible things between your limbs is something I find strengthening because I know that when I pick the right guy, I can let him have it. Some women feel oppressed by make-up and clothing, and here’s to them, they have every right to feel that way as well.

— Lady Gaga for Stylist

description.plain:
“The Cure” is a feel-good anthem about unconditional love for someone.

During her first live performance of this song at Coachella 2017, Gaga told the crowd:

I love you guys so much. I have been through so much in my life and I’ve seen so much. And you cure me every time with your love”

That performance was the debut of the song, which was released on streaming platforms and iTunes shortly after.

In early March 2017, Gaga was spotted venturing back into the recording studio. Many fans speculated a follow up to 2016’s Joanne was in the works, until the release of “The Cure.” Gaga confessed before premiering the song at Coachella that she “had trouble keeping the next part of her show a secret”.

The song is highly speculated to be written in tribute to Gaga’s dear friend, Sonja Durham, who was battling a losing fight with cancer at that time and sadly passed away a few months later.

As seen in Gaga’s documentary Five Foot Two, she gets a call from Sonja telling her things were going worse. Gaga tells her to stay strong, and that she will be with her right away, cancelling her other work-related plans. After hanging up, she tears up and says “I’m losing everyone I love”.

She might not have the Cure to Sonja’s cancer, but she will do her best to make her feel loved and cherished during her last days.

description.plain:
“Born This Way” is about self-liberation, and loving every part of yourself, no matter your race, gender, or sexuality; the song was released as the lead single from the album of the same name in February 2011.

In it, Lady Gaga emphasizes that loving a human or a religious entity can both equally be considered expressions of worship, as many religious people claim the importance of loving humans to be an essential part of their religion. With her lyrics, GaGa addresses the persistent prejudice against many types of love, e.g. non-heterosexual love that is still wide-spread among many religious communities and societies. GaGa criticizes any stance based on religious prejudice: to her, worshipping God equals loving all “His” creatures just the way they are.

The entire song is about internalizing this accepting point of view, learning who you are and loving that person.

The song was a huge success upon release, charting atop the Billboard Hot 100 for 6 straight weeks (as the 1000th No. 1 song).

Gaga’s anthem resembles Madonna’s 1989 hit “Express Yourself,” which was an (uncredited) homage to The Staple Singers‘ 1971 smash “Respect Yourself.”

This song, as Rolling Stone points out, also bears similarities to Patrick Hernandez’s 1978 disco tune “Born to Be Alive.”

description.plain:
“Applause” is an EDM/electro-pop celebration of sticking it to the haters, doing what one loves, and embracing the thrill of the crowd. Bed-ridden and forced to cancel tour dates due to a 2013 hip injury, Gaga yearned for the love – * the applause* – of her fans, inspiring her to write this song.

The song is the lead single off of Lady Gaga’s ARTPOP. It’s less robust than her previous lead singles, like “Bad Romance” and “Born This Way”, but what it lacks in length it displays in nightclub-ready energy and unapologetic campiness.

The song’s cover art is possibly Bowie-influenced.

description.plain:
“Venus” is a disco-influenced sex song, space-style. It’s one large triple entendre.

It’s definitely stranger than Applause, using many beat cuts and shifts, and unpredictable melody changes. Lady Gaga herself produced it.

It was intended to be the 2nd single for ARTPOP, but that honor was taken by Do What U Want, demoting this to the 1st promotional single.



One of the single covers for “Venus” allude to the “venus” that girls have, in a rather bizarre way. Combined with the ARTPOP album cover, it establishes feminism as a recurring theme.

description.plain:
Though “Perfect Illusion” first seems like a straightforward song about a failed love affair, Lady Gaga actually wrote it about the pitfalls of living in the age of social media. In the song, she expresses her disillusionment with the glossy, highly constructed versions of themselves that social media users project to their followers, as well as the way that her own larger-than-life persona prevents her from having authentic interactions with her fans. This anthem presents a vision for people to steer away from that behavior in order to re-establish genuine human connections.

The song served as the lead single from Gaga’s fifth solo studio album. It’s her first pop single since the 2013-2014 ARTPOP album era. Gaga wrote it on a typewriter.

Lady Gaga announced “Perfect Illusion” on her Instagram on August 17, 2016, in a series of individual panels forming the words “LADY GAGA / PERFECT ILLUSION / NEW SINGLE / SEPTEMBER.”

Three months before the announcement, producer Mark Ronson shared a cryptic photo of Gaga with the other producers—Tame Impala frontman Kevin Parker and BLOOD—captioned “Illusion.”

description.plain:
The second single from The Fame Monster, “Telephone” was originally written by Gaga for Britney Spears‘ Circus album, but Spears rejected it. Later, Gaga recorded the song as a collaboration with Beyoncé.

Gaga said, “I wrote it for her [Spears] a long time ago and she just didn’t use it for her album. It’s fine because I love the song and I get to perform it now.” Additionally, the guest vocalist was originally going to be Spears, but ultimately Gaga made Knowles the featured vocalist instead.

The main inspiration behind the song was Gaga’s fear of suffocation as she felt that she seldom found time to just let loose and have fun.

“Fear of suffocation—something that I have or fear is never being able to enjoy myself, … ‘Cause I love my work so much, I find it really hard to go out and have a good time. … I don’t go to nightclubs, … You don’t see pictures of me falling out of a club drunk. I don’t go—and that’s because I usually go and then, you know, a whiskey and a half into it, I got to get back to work.”

The song was accompanied by an epic, 9-minute music video which was the sequel to the equally epic “Paparazzi” video, and was heavily inspired by the work of Quentin Tarantino and others.

description.plain:
“Gypsy” was debuted in Germany. before performing the song, Gaga had this to say to the audience about the song:

So I wrote [“Gypsy”] when I was travelling around the world. And it was about this exact thing that you said to me…a gypsy doesn’t have a home. But I [a gypsy] do have a home. I have a home with you [all] always. This is my 1st performance of this record, it’s very special to me. Thank you for sharing it with me.

All in all, “Gypsy” is an autobiographical sort of song for Gaga, representing her life after becoming an entertainer and romanticizing the idea of travelling the world like a gypsy: never grounded, never held down.

description.plain:
In an interview with Daily Telegraph, Gaga said that “Paparazzi” is about “struggling to balance success and love.”

An excerpt from a separate interview:

The song is about a few different things–it’s about my struggles, do I want fame or do I want love? It’s also about wooing the paparazzi to fall in love with me. It’s about the media whoring, if you will, watching ersatzes make fools of themselves to their station. It’s a love song for the cameras, but it’s also a love song about fame or love–can you have both, or can you only have one?

The music video for the song was released in 2008 with controversial reception. It won two MTV Music Video Awards in 2009 for Best Art Direction and Special Effects, where she also carried out one of her most talked about performances to date.

description.plain:
“Alice” pays homage to the 1865 novel Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland, later popularized by the 1951 animated film adaptation. The tale sees young Alice fall asleep and wake up in a conceptualized fantastical world, brimming with imaginary, anthropomorphic characters, each representing an obstacle in life to overcome.

Throughout the track, Gaga connects her inability to find peace in her life to Alice’s need to survive the hardships of growing up and maintaining peace-of-mind.

The track was originally thought to be about Gaga’s childhood dog Alice, who passed away in 2013, however, Gaga denied this after revealing several lyrics in an interview with Zane Lowe.

description.plain:
“Alejandro” was the third single released from Lady Gaga’s EP The Fame Monster, following her blockbuster debut album The Fame. In some markets, The Fame Monster was issued with The Fame as a re-release.

The song showcases her sense of cynicism towards deciding if Alejandro (or any of the men mentioned in the song) are the one. The song is sonically inspired by Swedish pop groups ABBA  & Ace of Base. Gaga, speaking about The Fame Monster, said:

…I realized that I had written each song about a particular fear that I had come across on my journey promoting the fame….
Many interpret Alejandro as her lamentation of it.

Alejandro’s nine-minute video, directed by photographer Steven Klein, features totalitarian imagery and plays upon imagery from the 1930’s. The hispanic consonance of the names referred to in the song might lead one to think it’s about Franco’s Regime. But it is also said that the video references the treatment of homosexuals in Nazi Germany & the Weimar Republic. These references are rooted in imagery from the 1972 Bob Fosse film Cabaret.

Speaking to Larry King on Larry King Live in 2010, Gaga spoke of the music video saying it’s:

… a celebration of my love and appreciation for the gay community. My admiration of their bravery and their love for one another, their courage in their relationships. It’s something I have yet to – yet to nail on the head with a man…"

description.plain:
“Stupid Love” is a high-spirited electro-pop track where Lady Gaga can be heard singing about falling for someone and irrefutably wanting their love. This is the lead single from Gaga’s sixth studio album, Chromatica.

A mysterious snippet of the song surfaced on August 20, 2019 on Twitter, which was seemingly confirmed when the user who posted the snippet received a copyright claim from Universal Music Group three days later, confirming the song’s title. Further speculation arose when Gaga was seen listening to the track on her iPod in an Instagram post on October 29, 2019.

Adding fuel to the fire, The Sun published an article claiming Gaga’s lead single will be released on February 7, which was quickly refuted by her team on January 16, 2020. Two days later,  an extended snippet leaked via Snapchat, resulting in “Stupid Love” trending on Twitter, which led to the song’s full leak on January 21, 2020.

After much speculation regarding the track’s official release, Gaga finally confirmed it would be released on February 28th, 2020 at 12:00 AM EST.

The music video, directed by Daniel Askill was shot in Trona Pinnacles, California using Apple’s iPhone 11 Pro triple camera system.

description.plain:
“John Wayne” describes the singer’s attraction to rugged, cowboy-types that are the opposite of the city boys she usually encounters in Manhattan.

Lady Gaga gave her debut performance of the song live at the 2016 Victoria Secret Fashion Show, sporting an all black ensemble and her own pair of custom wings. The song was performed as a medley with “A-YO.”

The official video debuted on February 8th, 2017, exclusively on Apple Music.

description.plain:
“Free Woman” is the fifth track on Chromatica. The song was rumoured to be the first promo single as its demo leaked in full on May 8, 2020.

Among speculations about a possible arrival of her feat with Ariana Grande, “Rain On Me”, and the alleged second single from the album, “Free Woman”, it was the second one that leaked, showing a little more of the album’s electronic proposal, here inspired by house music.

During an episode of her podcast “Gaga Radio” in August 2020, she revealed that the album was almost named after the song, but she decided to change direction and continue with Chromatica as she didn’t feel like the idea of a “free woman” truly embodied her. She added:

Remember we were gonna call the album Free Woman? And I said, “Well, if we’re gonna call the album Free Woman, we should take a photo of me on a porch with prison bars around it.”

description.plain:
“Just Dance” is an upbeat track about Lady Gaga being at a party, getting incredibly drunk, and dancing it off. The song was released as Gaga’s debut single and became her first hit from her debut studio album, The Fame.

It’s meant to make people in difficult situations feel good about themselves, despite the fact that Colby’s solo and the bridge have heavy sexual reference.

“Just Dance” was effortless—it only took ten minutes to write, which is ironic considering its quick rise to fame (no pun intended).

The song was originally written for girl group The Pussycat Dolls for their sophomore album Doll Domination, along with several other tracks during Gaga’s initial career as a songwriter for Interscope Records artists. The songs were however, rejected before recording as confirmed by lead singer Nicole Scherzinger.

description.plain:
“Is That Alright?” is taken from Lady Gaga and Bradley Cooper’s ‘A Star is Born’. Though the song is not featured entirely in the movie, it plays at the end of the film and has a place on the movie’s soundtrack.

The song is character Ally’s ode to her husband, Jackson Maine. Lyrically, the piece depicts how Ally (Lady Gaga) wants to spend the rest of her life with Jackson – she wants to die with him. As such, the song is a musical expression of the marriage (‘till death do us part’) between these characters.

description.plain:
In ‘Replay’ Lady Gaga brings back all her allegories of ‘Monster’. Both from the song ‘Monster’ off of The Fame Monster Deluxe but also from what she has always embodied Monsters as: her fans.

‘He ate my heart’ she laments in the 2009 track, ‘Am I still alive? The monster inside you is torturing me’ she continues on this new track, more than a decade later, going full circle on exploring how trauma has affected her life.

The approach this time around can be see as a bit more different: more resigned, the dance-y melody in the background transports her and us and makes it feel like it’s ok. The music will get us through this, just dance, as a juxtaposition to the ‘Monster’ 2009 track where instead we could see a more scared, naive version of Gaga approaching trauma.

On Gaga’s Spotify storyline she clarifies how she sees a trauma that plagued her as a driving force for being braver “But really Chromatica cannot exist without an abstract explanation of what it’s like to be triggered if you have PTSD.”

description.plain:
Scheiße (alternate legal titles: “Scheisse”, “ScheiBe”, and “Shiza”) is a song written in 2010 by Lady Gaga and produced by RedOne.

The title and parts of the song are in German. Scheiße means shit/dammit in English.

The song was written a day after going to a “dirty party” in Berlin, and that it was about “wanting to be bad without permission.” The German that she speaks in the song is actually gibberish, which is the whole point of the song. Whenever people tell Gaga that she can’t be a strong woman, it all just sounds like gibberish, or bullshit/scheiße, to her.

description.plain:
“Dope” is a song by American recording artist Lady Gaga. It is the only ballad on her third album, ARTPOP.

During her performance at the 2013 iTunes Festival (dubbed Swinefest by the Lady herself) she played an early version of the song with different lyrics called “I Wanna Be With You”.

Lady Gaga promoted “Dope” before its release by wearing a snapback featuring the word DOPE, as well as posting its lyrics on Instagram, triggering the social media website’s concern.



“Dope” peaked at #8 on the Billboard Hot 100 due to a boost from Gaga’s performance of the song at the YouTube Music Awards.

The song was revealed with the tracklist of Lady Gaga’s sixth studio album, Chromatica.

description.plain:
“Yoü and I” is a song written by Lady Gaga in 2010 from her third album, Born This Way. The song describes her relationship with Lüc Carl, her main love interest at the time the song was written (the title is stylized after his name). She considered him to be the “love of her life,” and she has stated that every love song on her first three albums are about him.

The song samples the drums Queen’s “We Will Rock You”, and even features the band’s legendary guitarist Brian May.

description.plain:
The title track is Gaga’s manifesto of art and pop coming together. The line in chorus “We could belong together (ARTPOP)” refers to art and pop being one, just like herself and her Little Monsters. The blending of art and pop is happening here and throughout the album.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Art is meant to provoke different reactions to its audience, so there’s never essentially one true meaning. People try so hard to find one “true” meaning to LG’s various songs and music videos. Her POP songs and POP music videos are “her ART.” This is LG’s simple answer to anyone that asks what all of her songs and music videos even mean. They could mean anything. Everything she creates (songs, visuals, music videos) can and will mean a different way to each person, just like how art is meant to be.

description.plain:
“Joanne” is the title track off of Lady Gaga’s 2016 studio album, Joanne. In an interview with Zane Lowe for Beats 1 on 15th September, 2016, Gaga called the track “the true heart and soul of the record.” The track’s title is a reference to Gaga’s late aunt, Joanne Stefani Germanotta, who passed away on 18th December, 1974 from lupus at 19 years old. According to Gaga, her late aunt was a painter and a poet, and Gaga feels a need to continue her legacy through her music—to, in her own words, “finish [Joanne’s] business” by making it as an artist.

Gaga has frequently cited Joanne as an inspiration, telling Billboard, “I never met her, but she’s been one of the most important figures in my life,” and including a poem written by Joanne in the booklet for her 2008 breakout album, The Fame.

description.plain:
“Swine” is a song from Lady Gaga’s album ARTPOP. The EDM song is a callout to the people in life that use others. Never one to shy away from a meta reference, Gaga’s song is both the rejection of an abusive lover and a celebration of the “inner-swine” in her – and everyone. Gaga often uses dance music in her work to help others dance through their own problems, such as troubled love, rough nights out, or patriarchal, heteronormative societal pressures (e.g. “Bad Romance”, “Just Dance”, or “Scheiße”)

In 2014, on the Howard Stern Show, she said the following:

The song is about rape. The song is about demoralization. The song is about rage and fury and passion and I had a lot of pain that I wanted to release.

She revealed the song title in a V Magazine interview when she subtly corrected Marina Abramovic on the song’s name. It also gave the official nickname for Gaga’s iTunes Festival session, #SwineFest.

“I’ll Never Love Again” is the final song in the soundtrack for 2018’s A Star Is Born.

In the song, Ally (Lady Gaga) sings about her late husband Jackson (Bradley Cooper) who recently committed suicide in their garage while Ally performed her final concert on the tour.

It is later revealed that this song (which was written by Jack) was intended to be a duet with Ally. However, due to the embarrassment of Ally at the Grammy’s earlier in the movie, the song had no chance of boosting Ally’s popularity.

description.plain:
Being one of the biggest pop stars that debuted in the past decade, Lady Gaga has been praised for her whimsical artistic style. On this track, Gaga compares herself to a “plastic doll” that fits all the archetypes of what a perfect popstar should be like.

Gaga acknowledges that she knows that she fits into the archetype and has contributed to the objectification of artists in pop culture. However, Gaga admits that it hurts when society dehumanizes artists.

The themes of the song are similar to Gaga’s track, “Do What U Want” which also alluded to the idea of being “plastic” and separating her mind from her physical body.

Lady Gaga told Zane Lowe on Beats1 Radio that “Diamond Heart” is about chasing the American dream, and doing whatever it takes to achieve it. It references Gaga’s personal experience as a go go dancer, one of the jobs she had before she was famous.

The title, “Diamond Heart,” is a reference to her engagement ring from former fiancé Taylor Kinney, who proposed to her on Valentine’s Day with a diamond ring that is shaped like a heart.

description.plain:
Lady Gaga wrote this song after her dad had received heart surgery. He called her claiming he was “ready to die” and she was so distraught by his comment, that she wrote a song for/about him. She then played it to him live while they drank shots of whisky at the piano.

Gaga recorded this performance and used it as the very first “Speechless” demo, that she played for her label who asked her to record it professionally with producer Ron Fair.

Each song from Lady Gaga’s second album, The Fame Monster, represent one of her fears in life. “Speechless” is her ‘Fear of Death Monster."

description.plain:
“Hey Girl” features English musician Florence Welch, lead vocalist of the indie rock band Florence and The Machine. The collaboration, the only one on the album, was first announced on 9th September, 2016 during an interview with UK radio station BBC Radio 1 about the lead single from the album, “Perfect Illusion.”

The structure of “Hey Girl” is unique within Gaga’s catalogue and sees Welch and Gaga exchanging lines, one after the other. The duo hit back at critics who feel the need to pit successful women against one another, promoting the idea that, by supporting one another, women can fight back against sexist stigma.

description.plain:
The first song on the album Born This Way. The song was going to be the first single but the title track was chosen instead. The song later on became the 5th and final single of the album. It was written and produced by Lady Gaga and Fernando Garibay as Gaga was performing on the Monster Ball Tour.

On the surface song is about Gaga partying with her friends in New York. On a deeper level, however, the song is about Gaga “marrying” her insecurities, and finding enough bravery to go out and take the world by storm.

“Every song on all my albums has some relationship to New York City, but one in particular, ‘Marry the Night’, that record is about my husband New York.”

“Monster” represents the Fear of Sex Monster from the series of 8 new songs in Lady Gaga’s re-release of The Fame.

This song is reflective of the times in which Gaga was not able to feel comfortable with having sex.

In 2011, Gaga explained:

I did not lose my virginity until I was 17. But I have to say even then I wasn’t ready and it was an absolutely terrible experience. It was not good at all. […] I never actually enjoyed sex until two years ago. It was a proper monogamous relationship in which I felt free enough to trust and I had enough self love.

description.plain:
“The Edge of Glory” is a song by Lady Gaga, which was released as the third single from her album, Born This Way. The song was written as dedication to Gaga’s grandfather.

“The Edge of Glory” features a saxophone solo by Clarence Clemons, recorded as one of his last works before his untimely death in 2011, a month after the release of the single.

The song was relatively a success, reaching a peak of number three on the Billboard Hot 100 and marking Gaga’s 10th consecutive top ten hit on the chart.

The music video that accompanies Edge of Glory is one of Gaga’s simplest, and features her by herself in a Gianni Versace outfit dancing and walking around an empty street and a fire escape, illuminated by red and violet light.

description.plain:
“Angel Down” explains Gaga’s feelings towards the world of today, as well as her spirituality.

Gaga was inspired by the tragic murder of African-American teenager Trayvon Martin in 2012. Trayvon, walking unarmed, was shot by George Zimmerman, a neighborhood watch captain. The case was heavily publicized and instigated debates on racism, self-defense laws, and gun control. Unfortunately, Zimmerman was found not guilty.

Gaga confirmed her inspiration via Twitter:

https://twitter.com/ladygaga/status/788895376296271872

Gaga has always talked openly about her connection to her religion. During the process of making Joanne, she showed her involvement with the Catholic Church on social media, posting the following picture with a priest from her family’s church on Instagram:

https://www.instagram.com/p/BFKD-mqJFEe/


Thank you Father Duffell for a beautiful homily as always and lunch at my pop’s restaurant.

I was so moved today when you said.. “The Eucharist is not a prize for the perfect but the food that God gives us.” – Father Duffell, Blessed Sacrament Church  Nourishment. .


The track, a mid-tempo ballad, is the final track on the standard edition of Gaga’s fourth solo album, Joanne, which was released on the 21st October 2016.

description.plain:
“Grigio Girls” is a very personal ballad about the support system that blossomed around Sonja Dunham, Lady Gaga’s personal friend and Haus of Gaga’s managing director, who is fighting against cancer. Gaga has said that the track is about “womanhood and sticking together and encouraging one another and teaching each other that it’s ok to cry together.” On Friday, May 19th, 2017, Sonja’s husband, Andre Dubois, confirmed the sad news that Sonja had lost her battle with cancer.

Gaga first posted about Sonja’s struggle on her social network Little Monsters, writing:

True friendship is giving each other lymphatic drainage massage in infrared sauna. Me and Sonja Durham, Haus of Gaga member fighting stage four breast cancer with lots of compassion and love.

description.plain:
“Just Another Day” is the only song on Joanne that Lady Gaga wrote by herself. On October 4th, she teased the lyrics and some info about the song during an interview with On Air With Ryan Seacrest. She said:

[“Just Another Day” is] probably the most New York-glam-pop song on the album. It’s the one that airs from [David Bowie], Mark Bolan, and then maybe from some like obscure, London metal stuff, the Beatles. It also kind of airs from the electro-clash movement from New York and that’s kind of when I started coming up, was right after that.

On October 20th, during the second date of her Dive Bar Tour, Gaga spoke about how she came up with the song, saying it is about her friendship with Mark Ronson, and imagining what they would have been like if they’d known each other as kids growing up in New York. Mark Ronson was close friends with Sean Lennon, and Lady Gaga, who actually lived nearby, would sometimes catch Yoko Ono leaving flowers at John Lennon’s “Imagine” memorial. The resulting track has some The Beatles vibes, and this may be the reason.

description.plain:
“Americano” is a song off Born This Way, and stands out for both its Latin influences and lesbian love story. This was her first proper collaboration with Fernando Garibay and White Shadow.

During an interview with Vogue, Gaga described the song as:

A big mariachi techno-house record, where I am singing about immigration law and gay marriage and all sorts of things that have to do with disenfranchised communities in America…It sounds like a pop record, but when I sing it, I see Edith Piaf in a spotlight with an old microphone."

This song was written as a response to Proposition 8 and Arizona immigration laws.

description.plain:
Accompanied by a somber background of stringed instruments, Lady Gaga powerfully sings a song of empathy. This masterful ballad was co-written by Diane Warren for the 2015 film The Hunting Ground, and gained an Oscar nomination for Best Original Song.

The Hunting Ground is a documentary-style movie following sexual assault cases and rape crimes committed on college campuses across the United States. Gaga was asked to lend her vocals to the cause in order to bring awareness to the issue.

In 2014, Gaga revealed that she is also a victim of sexual assault; lending a haunting perspective to these emotionally charged lyrics.

description.plain: “Hair” is a song from Lady Gaga’s second studio album “Born This Way”. The song starts out with a slow piano melody which then turns into a dance beat influenced by rock music. The saxophone played by Clarence Clemons from the E Street Band is reminiscent of the 80s. It is also a throwback at Gaga’s childhood. The title of the song is a metaphor for identity and freedom.

description.plain:
“Teeth” represents the Fear of Truth Monster from the series of 8 new songs in Lady Gaga’s re-release of The Fame.

In an interview with MTV News, Gaga revealed more about the song’s context:

It is meant to mean two things: the first one kind of juvenile sexual provocative connotation is about oral sex, but also the monster in the song is fear of the truth. “Show me your teeth” means “tell me the truth” and I think that for a long time in my life that I replaced sex with the truth.

The oral theme is prevalent throughout the song by the use of the words “fangs” “bite” and “mouth” (aside from “teeth” itself).

Lady Gaga recorded “Boys Boys Boys” in 2007, produced by RedOne. The song was supposed to be the next single after Paparazzi, but was canceled due to the earlier-than-expected release of Bad Romance.

Lady Gaga has stated that she wanted to create her version of Mötley Crüe’s “Girls Girls Girls.”. Also, Lady Gaga has described this song in early interviews as “a metal song trapped in a pop star’s body.”

description.plain:
“Eh, Eh (Nothing Else I Can Say)” is a synth-pop ballad from Lady Gaga’s debut studio album, The Fame. It was released as a single from the LP in several countries, but not in the United States. The official music video premiered on February 3rd, 2009. (Watch it by pressing play above!)

A quote from Gaga about the track:

‘Eh, Eh’ is my simple pop song about finding someone new and breaking up with the old boyfriend.

It’s also rumored that the inspiration for the song came when two guys she was dating met and all she had to say was … “Eh, eh.”

songs.lyrics:
"The Prelude Pathétique"- First Part:
When I look back on my life it’s not that I don’t want to see things exactly as they happened, it’s just that I prefer to remember them in an artistic way. And truthfully the lie of it all is much more honest because I invented it. Clinical psychology tells us arguably that trauma is the ultimate killer. Memories are not recycled like atoms and particles in quantum physics. They can be lost forever. It’s sort of like my past is an unfinished painting and as the artist of that painting I must fill in all the ugly holes, and make it beautiful again. It’s not that I have been dishonest; it’s just that I loathe reality

For example those nurses, they're wearing next season Calvin Klein and so am I. And the shoes custom Giuseppe Zanotti. I tipped their gause caps to the side like Parisian berets because I think it's romantic, and I also think that mint will be very big in fashion next spring

Check out this nurse on the right; she's got a great ass. Bam

The truth is back at the clinic they only wore those funny hats to keep the blood out of their hair. And that girl on the left she ordered gummy bears and a knife a couple of hours ago, they only gave her the gummy bears. I'd wish they'd only given me the gummy bears

"The Prelude Pathétique"- Last Part:
You may say "I lost everything". But I still had my Be-Dazzler. And I had a lot of patches, shiny ones from M&J Trimming. So I wreaked havoc on some old denim. And I did what any girl would do; I did it all over again

description.plain:
“Paper Gangsta” is a song written by Lady Gaga and producer RedOne from Gaga’s debut album, The Fame in 2008.

Almost every artist in the beginning accept label deals that don’t give any credit (neither a penny) for them. Lady Gaga suffered this with her previous label Def Jam. The song relates to Gaga’s feeling about her six month record deal with Island Def Jam in 2006-2007.

In 2010, the song was used in the music video for “Telephone”, it is playing on a stereo set towards the beginning of the video.

description.plain:
This dialogue is a cover of the introductory verse of “Over the Rainbow” from the theatrical version of The Wizard of Oz, although the verse was omitted from the movie version of the production.

This choice of introductory dialogue is likely no accident as it pays ode to the original singer, Judy Garland who starred as Vicky Lester (synonymous with Gaga’s character, Ally) in the 1954 version of A Star Is Born.

Interestingly, Barba Streisand – who played the leading role in the 1976 version of A Star Is Born – also famously covered this song.

This song perfectly sets the tone for the movie, with the message of hope for a better future. This is the core theme that underlies the motive of both leading characters throughout the movie.

description.plain:
Keeping in theme with the opener, “Chromatica II” is a string instrumental interlude. The track appears one-third of the way through the album introducing the second part of the journey.

The Spotify description of the track reads,

I believe it’s in the middle of our voyages as people that things become both terrifying and whimsical at the same time. I felt life was asking the impossible of me, which I think I’m not alone in feeling. So I was scared, but I believe in magic. So, I wrote this interlude as a reminder that my magic was working. I believe that means yours is too.

description.plain:
Performed by Elton John and written alongside long time collaborator Bernie Taupin, this 70s hit song served as the B-side to the single “Take Me to the Pilot.” However, due to the popularity of the song with disc jockeys at the time, the song was made to be the A-side instead.

The song has been covered by many artists over the years, including Lady Gaga—and as the godmother of Elton John’s children and a good friend of his, her rendition of the song has been featured on the Revamp album.



“Your Song” was first released on October 26, 1970 and was Elton’s first pop hit peaking at #8 of the Billboard Hot 100 chart. Gaga has sung renditions of “Your Song” at the 52nd Grammy Awards and the I’m Still Standing – A Grammy Salute, two days after the 60th Grammy Awards.

Revamp was released on April 6, 2018 as one of the two tribute albums dedicated to Sir Elton John.

The song has an industrial techno production that represents the blueprint for Born This Way .

I Like It Rough is a song written by Lady Gaga and Martin Kierszenbaum, for her debut album, The Fame, sometime between 2007-2008. The song was first released as a bonus track for the Canadian/Australian edition, and later became a standard track on other releases of the album.

The song was written about addiction and in particular “masochist love” — being in love with people that are not good for you. The song deal about Lady Gaga’s ex-boyfriend in a reflection about “Why does she likes it rough ?”. The demo of the song was titled as “I Like It Ruff”.

description.plain:
“Beautiful, Dirty, Rich” is a track from Lady Gaga’s debut studio album, The Fame. The song was released as a promotional single.

Although it was met minimal commercial success, critics complimented Gaga on the fun lyrics and nature, especially with its accompanying 2008 music video.

In an interview, Gaga talked about what the song means to her:

On the Lower East side, there was a lot of rich kids who did drugs and said that they were poor artists, so it’s also a knock at that. […] But ultimately what I want people to take from it is “Bang-bang.” No matter who you are and where you come from, you can feel beautiful and dirty rich.

The song was featured at the start of an episode of Skins (U.K.).

Summerboy is a song written by Lady Gaga and KNS Productions, who also produced it in 2007. The song is on Lady Gaga’s debut album, The Fame.

The inspiration behind the song could be about a romantic fling or the transience of stardom. It lends itself to what is almost a Grease reference.

In an interview revealed that one of the inspiration behind the song was dating a guy in the summer when you know the relationship won’t last beyond it. According to Gaga, most girls fall in love during the summer when clothes are off.

description.plain:
“PARTYNAUSEOUS” is a song written by Lady Gaga in 2012 and was due to be released as a collaboration on Kendrick Lamar’s album good kid m.A.A.d. city. The song was scheduled to be released on iTunes on September 6, 2012, one month before the album. The release was later scrapped due to creative differences between Gaga and Lamar’s teams. The song was later used as an interlude on the ARTPOP Ball in 2014. Supposedly, there is an alternate version featuring Jaden C.

A high quality version of the one used during the ARTPOP Ball leaked its way onto the internet on September 5th, 2018.

description.plain:
Though it is simply a piano ballad revision, this version of Lady Gaga’s title track off of her latest album Joanne brings back into the light the issues of lupus, a body-deteriorating disease where the immune system attacks its own tissues. The song is written for Gaga’s aunt Joanne who died from the disease, and along with the announcement of this song’s release, she revealed that a donation would be made to the Lupus Research Alliance and urged others to donate as well.

It’s not certain if the song will be a single, but with the success of her piano-driven “Million Reasons,” that could be a driving force behind releasing it as such. Fans also speculate it to be performed at this year’s upcoming Grammy Awards.

body.plain:
Though it is simply a piano ballad revision, this version of Lady Gaga’s title track off of her latest album Joanne brings back into the light the issues of lupus, a body-deteriorating disease where the immune system attacks its own tissues. The song is written for Gaga’s aunt Joanne who died from the disease, and along with the announcement of this song’s release, she revealed that a donation would be made to the Lupus Research Alliance and urged others to donate as well.

It’s not certain if the song will be a single, but with the success of her piano-driven “Million Reasons,” that could be a driving force behind releasing it as such. Fans also speculate it to be performed at this year’s upcoming Grammy Awards.

On January 10th, 2019, the song officially won for the 2019 Grammy’s under the category for “Best Pop Solo Performance”.

description.plain:
“Lush Life” is a jazz standard with lyrics and music written by Billy Strayhorn from 1933 to 1938. The song’s lyrics describe the author’s weariness of the night life after a failed romance, wasting time with “jazz and cocktails” at “come-what-may places” and in the company of girls with “sad and sullen gray faces/distinque traces”. Strauhorn was only 16 when he wrote the majority of the song, which was to become his signature composition (along with “Take the ‘A’ Train”).

Lady Gaga covered the song for their upcoming collaborative album, Cheek to Cheek. The single is a pure jazz, with piano at the background as the lead instrumentation.
It was debuted live.

description.plain: “Nothing On (But the Radio)” is an unreleased song that was written by Lady Gaga in 2010. The title is a reference to a Marilyn Monroe quote, which was a response to her nude photographs, to which she said, “It’s not true that I had nothing on, I had the radio on.” The song leaked online in 2012. In 2016, a Youtube video featuring Paris Monroe of Destinee & Paris surfaced. The video featured a snippet of Paris Monroe’s version of “Nothing On (But the Radio), leading people to speculate that the song may have been sold to Paris.

description.plain:
Retro, Dance, Freak is a song written by Lady Gaga, Rob Fusari, and Calvin Gaines in September-November of 2006.

It was first released on the Japan and Brazil pressing of The Fame, then being released on the Australian version. It was also released on the deluxe edition of The Fame Monster. It replaced the bonus track, “Again Again” on the Australian and Polish version of the The Fame Monster.

The title of the song was used to describe herself on her PureVolume page back in 2006. The name might have also come from the retro sounding dance beat in her earlier songs and her feelings of being a freak when she was younger.

“Rain on Me (Solo Demo)“ is the demo version of Lady Gaga & Ariana Grande’s song  “Rain on Me”. Unlike the final version of the song, the demo does not feature Ariana Grande and replaces her second verse with a new verse from Gaga. The song also features a new lyric from Gaga at the end of the first verse, as well as an unidentified male voice during the post-choruses.

The demo version appeared online on May 22, 2020.

description.plain:
“Second Time Around” is a song written by The JAM and Lady Gaga in 2008. While it is clear that Gaga never intended to use the song herself, it is unclear who the song was actually written for. Some suggest that the song was due to be recorded by Michael Bolton, as Gaga and The JAM wrote another song for him around the same time.

The song is about trying to revisit an old love and failing.

description.plain:
The first iteration of the song, without R. Kelly, was alluded to by Lady Gaga in a tweet:

https://twitter.com/ladygaga/status/295372525272178688?lang=en

When the single was released as part of the album countdown, these lyrics were replaced with a verse by R. Kelly.

It wasn’t until a performance on the Graham Norton Show that the original lyrics made an appearance:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vcSVO64H3iI

A angelic, acoustic version of the song was also performed on Alan Carr in December 2013, followed by another performance that month with Christiana Aguilera on “The Voice”.

Although the solo version was omitted from the official tracklist, it was released on iTunes as part of a Spanish compilation in April 2014.

description.plain:
“Fooled Me Again” is a song written by Lady Gaga and Rob Fusari. The song was intended for Lady Gaga’s debut album, The Fame, but did not make the final cut because it didn’t fit in with the main theme of the album. However, the song was used in promotional video of the album The Fame: Part One.

Lyrically, the song is about Gaga’s admiration for another guy, but she knows deep down inside that he isn’t good for her, but she keeps falling  over and over for him, and continuously getting “fooled”.

“We Could Be Lovers” is an unreleased song by Lady Gaga, allegedly intended for the soundtrack to the 2018 musical, “A Star Is Born” but it has yet to be confirmed by Gaga or her team.

The song leaked online on December 17, 2020.

description.plain: On March 25, 2011, Lady Gaga released an alternate version of Born This Way, called the “Country Road” edit. This version was also released as a gift to her fans (she has become the first person on Twitter with 9,000,000 followers). On April 5, 2011, the Country Road version was released on iTunes, with a portion of the proceeds going to benefit the the Gay, Lesbian and Straight Education Network (GLSEN).

description.plain: “Wonderful” was the first song Team Love Child (Gaga & Rob Fusari) and Tom Kafafian wrote together. Written in 2006 and was included on the demo tape she sent to Interscope Records before getting signed. In an interview Gaga said that she had no plans to release the song on an album but rather give it to upcoming artist Adam Lambert. But evidently, she gave Glambert “Fever” instead. This song is about being so in love with someone who doesn’t love you back. Daydreaming that one day that the person would find you “wonderful” and feel the same. In the song you can hear Gaga’s raw, true emotions in her vocals.

description.plain:
“Ratchet” was one of the 60 songs written for Lady GaGa’s third album ARTPOP that did not make the final cut.

It was used in her ‘ArtRave: The ARTPOP Ball’ Tour as an instrumental interlude with a quarter of the original chorus at the end.

DJ White Shadow later used the instrumental for his debut EP Clock Is Ticking.

songs.lyrics:
This is the manifesto of Mother Monster:

On GOAT, a government owned territory in space, a birth of magnificent and magical proportions took place. But the birth was not finite, it was infinite. As the wombs numbered and the mitosis of the future began it was perceived that this infamous moment in life is not temporal, it is eternal. And thus began the beginning of the new race; a race within the race of humanity; a race which bears no prejudice, no judgment but boundless freedom. But on that same day as the eternal Mother hovered in the multiverse another, more terrifying, birth took place: the birth of evil

And as she, herself, split into two, rotating in agony between two ultimate forces, the pendulum of choice began its dance. It seems easy, you imagine, to gravitate, instantly and unwaveringly, towards good but she wondered, “How can I protect something so perfect without evil?”

description.plain:
“Tea” (stylized as “TEA”) is a song written by Lady Gaga in 2012 for “ARTPOP.” She revealed the song title and some of the lyrics via Twitter:
https://twitter.com/ladygaga/status/256533045530746880?lang=en
Despite the song being confirmed to be on the album, it did not make it to the final cut.

In February of 2017, during a Q&A, DJWS confirmed that the song is still in his posession and compared it to Toxic by Britney Spears. He then said he would probably release it someday.

DJ White Shadow performed the intro to the song at the Joanne World Tour at Fenway Park in Boston on September 1, 2017 saying:

“I thought it was appropriate [to play "TEA”] since we’re in Boston. Let’s see what this does, man. It’s the intro to the song – I put a little bit of the song out but no vocals."

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T4H_8mN-taw

description.plain: “Greatest” is an unreleased Lady Gaga song, which leaked in 2011. The song was given to Cher in 2011 for her 26th album, Closer to the Truth, but the song did not make the album’s final cut. A rough demo featuring both Lady Gaga and Cher on the song, re-titled to “The Greatest Thing”, leaked online on August 13th, 2011.

description.plain:
This is the demo of Lady Gaga’s song “Sexxx Dreams” from her fourth album “ARTPOP”. It was originally named “Sex Dreams” and this demo was recorded around August 2013, the instrumental is almost finished (a little bit slower) and the lyrics are pretty the same (longer chorus), but the last bridge was finally deleted.
She sang this version at the iTunes Festival on September 1st, 2013.

body.plain:
This is the demo of Lady Gaga’s song “Sexxx Dreams” from her fourth album “ARTPOP”. It was originally named “Sex Dreams” and this demo was recorded around August 2013, the instrumental is almost finished (a little bit slower) and the lyrics are pretty the same (longer chorus), but the last bridge was finally deleted.
She sang this version at the iTunes Festival on September 1st, 2013.

description.plain: “Captivated” is a piano ballad song written by Lady Gaga and performed in 2005 for Ultraviolet Live, New York University’s annual talent show. She ended up coming in 3rd place, 2nd place was Funky Butter, and 1st place was Tom Costello & Stephan Magloire. She played the song along side “Electric Kiss”. The song was written particularly for this talent show. In April 2010, the song was registered on BMI. Lady Gaga performed the song at the Jerome Schottenstein Center during The Monster Ball Tour.

description.plain:
“No Floods” is a song written during the last trimester of 2005 by Lady Gaga. The title of the song was inspired by the victims of Hurricane Katrina.
There are two versions of the song, the first version is the demo, played with a guitar and piano. This version was released on the demo, Words. Gaga later re-recorded it with her band. This version was produced by Joe Vulpis, and was released on the extended play, Red and Blue.
There are multiple differences between the two versions. Not only the instrumental back-track, but the lyrics were also changed. Some of the lines were condensed, while new lines replaced others.

description.plain: “Onion Girl” is a song written by Lady Gaga and produced by Zedd in 2012 for ARTPOP. She revealed the song title on November 19, 2013 in an interview with Canadian radio station, KiSS 92.5. Dave Russel, who engineered the sound for ARTPOP, confirmed that Zedd’s track “Addicted To A Memory” actually uses the same instrumental as Onion Girl.[1] Zedd talked about this, where he says the email is fake but he never confirms that he didn’t reuse the track for the song, however, he confirms that there was another track before Onion Girl.

description.plain:
Information about the original version with Colby O'Donis and Akon can be seen here. Some radio stations play a version of the song without Colby O'Donis and Akon.

The first difference between this solo version, and the original version is that Colby O'Donis “Verse 3” is completely removed from the song. The usual Lady Gaga chorus that comes after it is removed as well. The song then just goes right into the bridge. The second difference is that there is an outro to the song with extra Lady Gaga ad-libs.

The song was originally written for girl group The Pussycat Dolls for their sophomore album Doll Domination, along with several other tracks during Gaga’s initial career as a songwriter for Interscope Records artists. The songs were however, rejected before recording as confirmed by lead singer Nicole Scherzinger.

description.plain:
“Kandy Life” is a song written by Lady Gaga and Rob Fusari (Team Love Child) in 2007.

The song was made available through her MySpace during the same year, but later removed.

It was included as one of five songs on a demo disc compiled by Gaga’s then manager, Laurent Becenson at the time of her performance at Lollapalooza in 2007. A copy of the disc sold on eBay in December 2009.

songs.lyrics:
[Spoken Monologue]
When I was younger, I was at some point, born.
I grew in both IQ and EQ and as that happened I discovered that I was living in two realities at once.
They fought all the time and yet I made space for both of them for a reason I can't explain.
One reality I experienced was my Earth reality. The day, today, painting of what I was taught was my natural state in life.
At the time I also experienced a dream simultaneously and this dream was in combat with my Earth reality at all times.
A vision where I perform my thoughts for the world, a world where I mattered in a different way.
A world where I was valued for different things.
And in this world I was kind and that kindness spread through people, through sound.
This was the birth of Chromatica.

Love is an element on Chromatica, like earth, wind, fire, water.
It's a natural force and it's the only way that I can organize this super organism that is the Earth, it's by making it one whole thing.
Where time and linear structure don't matter, they don't exist.
We are all love.
I am love.
So it's everything around us.
It's how we work.
It's the thing we both initiate and respond to.
It's why everything happens, both good and bad.
It's the only way that I can make things simple.
And why shouldn't it be simple?
I breathe in and out love.
I don't believe it to be a choice other than I choose to breathe.
That is Chromatica.
It is how I do hard things.
It's neither right nor wrong nor is it greater or less than any other perspective on life.
No one thing is greater than another.
Kindness rules all things.
It simply is and it's mine.
You can have it too, though.
My best friend says "Sharing is caring" but we both know that I don't need to share your perspective with you for us both to care.

The Manifesto of Chromatica it's never-ending, I cannot finish it here.
It would be declaring I would never make music or be Lady Gaga again, which would mean I would stop being myself.
This manifesto finale marks the new beginning of my life.
One where I acknowledge that sound is my life force and that Lady Gaga is the mystery that carries it.
Chromatica can't end, it's how I make sense of things.
That's what you should tell people if they ask you what it is.
And for what is worth I think we all need that to make sense of things even if at times it feels absurd.

In 2009, the song title was used on a t-shirt from the official store. The title of the song can be heard in “We Are Plastic”.

description.plain:
“Paradise” is a song written by Lady Gaga from her collaborative album with Tony Bennett, Cheek to Cheek. Bennett revealed the song title in an interview, stating that it is one of the original tracks written by Gaga for the album, but the song was not included on the final track list as Gaga was too nervous to put it on the album, since it was her first Jazz composition.

However, in an exclusive Q & A on Gaga Daily with fans, Gaga revealed that we might hear the song someday and that it’s inspired by her father’s sister and him, and the phrases as they are traded are meant to be their words to each other right before she died. She died very young, but she wrote a poem about Heaven right before it happened, and that’s why it’s called ‘Paradise’.

It was believed that the song would be released in “Joanne”, however it didin’t make the cut.

description.plain:
“Musicland” is an up-tempo piano pop song, written by Lady Gaga and Rob Fusari (Team Love Child).

The song was released shortly on Lady Gaga’s PureVolume page in 2006. On the same site, one of her digital EPs is titled Musicland.

The song was registered on ASCAP, but was removed sometime in 2008. However, it remains registered on Fusari’s ASCAP repertoire.

The song was going to be performed at The Much Music Awards 2009, but was removed from the setlist last-minute. GaGa also sound-checked a few lines of this song during some South Korean interview in 2008

description.plain:
“Little Monsters” is a song that Lady Gaga created for her special guest appearance on the U.S. television series “The Simpsons”.

The song goes on to say that people who are shunned out, outcasts or people who are different are a “monster” as they are called… but that it doesn’t have to be a bad thing. Everyone is beautiful in their own way and you don’t need materialistic items to be happy is what Lady Gaga sings.

The song is similar to her 2011 hit single “Born This Way” in terms of story.

body.plain:
The interview was taken live with Stephen Fry on the chat show Mr.Fry

Here posted the half of the interview. Do check out the whole video, and see what happens next!

songs.lyrics:
Stephen Fry: I know people talk to you about all the same things but one of the things I just wanted to talk to you about, because it’s so obvious coming here, is the thing I think that you always say is most important to you, which is the fans, and they’re all outside and I gather you took them out some hot chocolate?

Lady Gaga: Actually, well, I sent them hot chocolate yesterday and macaroons, and then today I had press all day and I felt bad because I usually would leave the hotel and I would go to say “hi” but I knew that I wouldn’t have time and they’d be waiting all day, so I just went down and I brought them some fresh cookies and flowers.

SF: Ooooh! And do you find there’s a difference between your fans in different countries or is there a sort of similarity: is there a kind of Gaga fan who has a commonality?

LG: Yes, there is. The little monsters are a community and it’s kind of nice that everywhere I go they create a little home for me.

SF: Both those who, I suppose, describe themselves as your critics and those who adore you, as I do I’m unashamed to say, would concentrate on the fact that you are quite happy to be self consciously a spokesman for the dispossessed, the marginal, the freakish, the outsider, the sexually different, the ugly, the fat, the one who doesn’t fit in, the one who feels outside the tribe, if you like.

LG: Yes, it could be anybody.
SF: Which, in fact, is most of us. None of us really feels we belong, just some of us are better at hiding it than others.
LG: I think so. Some of us wear the mask prouder than others.
SF: Yes. Exactly. And the title of this album is the one that most directly addresses that, I suppose, Born This Way and the title song of it.
LG: Yes. The album is about being able to be reborn over and over again throughout your life.
SF: Oh, so it’s not just that God made me gay or God made me lesbian or God made me bi, and that’s who I am?
LG: No.
SF: It’s about being reborn, is it?
LG: No, not really.

songs.lyrics:
I know that you all have been feeling a tremendous range of emotions. Since we've all have heard about this horrible, hateful attack on Orlando and on your and our community. As we have now witnessed the largest mass shooting in American history. I can't help but feel that this level of hatred, like all predigital crimes, this is an attack on humanity itself. This is an attack on everyone. Tonight I gather humbly with you. As a human being: in peace, in sincerity, in commitment, in solidarity. To take a real moment and mourn the tragic loss of these innocent, beautiful people. And let's all today pledge an allegiance of love to them, and to their families, who are suffering so deeply. They are sons and daughters, they're fathers and mothers, they are all our brothers and our sisters. But tonight I will not allow my anger and outrage over this attack to overshadow our need to honour those who are grieving truly for their lost ones. Lost members of the LGBT community. I hope you know that myself and so many are your allies. Not only me but everyone here, we represent the compassion and the loyalty of millions of people around the world that believe in you, you are not alone. You are not alone. Tomorrow I hope that we all raise thoughtfully and loudly towards solutions. But tonight and right now, Orlando, we are united with you and we are here to remember.

Edward Sotomayar Jr., 34
Stanley Almodovar III, 23
Luis Omar Ocasio-Capo, 20
Juan Ramon Guerrero, 22
Eric Ivan Ortiz-Rivera, 36
Peter O. Gonzalez-Cruz, 22
Luis S. Vielma, 22
Kimberly Morris, 37
